note: Owner edit list for Atlas job J6 (lens packs). Gulf lenses first, then world lenses. Lenses with a lensesJson id take their meaning, UI mappings and care rules from banana-server/lib/bend/lenses.json. The brief is a starting fact sheet for lenses that are not in lenses.json yet; the model must not go past what it can credit.

lenses.name: Hejazi roshan
lenses.brief: The roshan (plural rawasheen) is the projecting wooden window bay of the old houses of Hejaz, best known from Al-Balad in Historic Jeddah, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Turned and carved wooden lattice panels let breeze and light in, keep privacy, and stack up the tall coral stone facades in vertical rhythms. Credit the Hejazi builders and carpenters.

lenses.name: Square Kufic
lenses.brief: Square Kufic builds real words from straight strokes on a square grid. The motif tile must show only the grid construction (square modules and right-angle strokes), never letters, real or fake: real words are set later with the user.

lenses.name: Diwani calligraphy
lenses.brief: Diwani is a flowing, tightly packed cursive calligraphy style that grew in the Ottoman court chancery (the diwan) for decrees and official documents, and is used across the Arab world, including the Gulf, for formal invitations and certificates. Its grammar: rising slanted baselines, letters that stack and overlap, long sweeping curves. The motif tile must show only abstract curves and slanted baselines, never letters, real or fake: real words are set later with the user and a calligrapher.

lenses.name: AlUla sandstone strata
lenses.brief: AlUla in northwest Saudi Arabia is a landscape of layered sandstone cliffs, eroded outcrops and wide valleys. It holds Hegra (Al-Hijr), the first UNESCO World Heritage site in Saudi Arabia, with Nabataean tombs cut into the rock. The lens takes the geology: horizontal strata of different thickness, warm sand and rust tones, wind erosion that softens edges. Do not copy tomb facades as ornament and never use the ancient inscriptions as pattern.

lenses.name: Gulf dhow building
lenses.brief: Dhows are the wooden sailing vessels of the Gulf and the western Indian Ocean, built by hand by shipwrights in ports such as Kuwait, Bahrain, Sur in Oman and Dubai, and used for pearling, fishing and trade. Grammar: the curve of the hull planks, ribs set at a steady interval, the triangle of the lateen sail, rope lashing and carved stern panels. Credit the shipwrights and sailing communities of the Gulf.

lenses.name: Bauhaus
lenses.brief: The Bauhaus was a German art and design school (1919 to 1933, in Weimar, Dessau and Berlin) that joined craft and industry. Grammar: primary shapes (circle, square, triangle), primary colors with black, asymmetric layouts, sans serif type and visible construction.

lenses.name: Portuguese azulejo
lenses.brief: Azulejos are painted, tin-glazed ceramic tiles from Portugal, used on facades, churches and stations from the 15th century to today, best known in cobalt blue on white. Grammar: a square tile repeat that builds a larger pattern across many tiles, border tiles that frame a panel, hand-painted brush lines. Avoid religious scenes that appear on many church panels.

lenses.name: Moroccan zellige
lenses.brief: Zellige is Moroccan mosaic tilework: small hand-cut glazed terracotta pieces set into geometric star and polygon patterns, made by maalems (master craftsmen), with Fez as a well-known centre. Grammar: interlocking star and polygon geometry, many small pieces in a radial repeat, slight color variation between pieces. Never add sacred inscriptions.

lenses.name: Indian hand block printing
lenses.brief: Hand block printing is a textile craft of India, with well-known centres in Rajasthan such as Sanganer and Bagru, where printers stamp carved wooden blocks onto cloth in repeat, one color per block. Grammar: a small motif stamped in a strict grid or half-drop repeat, slight misregistration between colors, natural dye tones. Credit the printer communities.
